# S224 — Set the per-project bell with ork projects set --bell

`ork projects set NAME --bell on|off` writes the registry field `bell` through the daemon's `projects.set`, so the owner no longer edits `projects.json` by hand. It is the second half of S100 (the bell on run end and the field itself land there) and needs that slice first.

## Why

The owner decided on 2026-10-28 (interactive, S100 note) that the bell stays on by default and is switched per project with a registry field `bell`, set with `ork projects set NAME --bell on|off`. S100 stays out of `internal/daemon` so it can pair with an E-class slice (pair waves allow one slice whose Files touch `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or `cmd`, `docs/design.md`, search "at most one slice whose Files touch"). The setter cannot: `ork projects set` always goes through the daemon's `projects.set` (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:225-337`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:513`), so this slice is E-class and pairs with an N-class slice.

Behaviour (exact):
- Flag `--bell on|off`. Any other value is a usage error before the daemon starts (`projects set: --bell takes on or off, got "X"`), as `--push` is (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:252-259`).
- Wire field `bell`, a pointer to a boolean in `SetProjectParams` (`internal/daemon/wire.go:270-283`); `SetsNothing` counts it. `on` stores `true`, `off` stores `false`; there is no way back to "absent" other than `on`, which is the same behaviour.
- The call is refused with `project_busy` while the project has unfinished runs, like every other field of `projects.set` (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:571-577`). See the owner question in the manifest.
- Text output: `bell=on` or `bell=off` in the `updated NAME: ...` line, in flag order. JSON: `{"project":{...}}` carries `"bell":true|false` when set.
- The TUI reads the setting at start, so a running TUI needs a restart to apply it (S100).

## Failing tests

In `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go`:

- TestProjectsSetBell: `projects.set` with `{"name":"p","bell":false}` saves `bell:false` and the reply carries it; `{"bell":true}` saves `true`; other fields stay unchanged. Fails first: unknown field (`bad_params`).
- TestProjectsSetBellRefusesAnUnfinishedRun: with an unfinished run, `{"name":"p","bell":false}` is `project_busy` and the registry is unchanged.
- TestSetsNothingCountsBell: `SetProjectParams{Bell: &v}.SetsNothing()` is false.

In `internal/cli/cli_test.go`:

- TestProjectsSetBellOnOff: `ork projects set p --bell off` sends `bell:false` and prints `updated p: bell=off`; `--bell on` prints `bell=on`; `--json` carries the project.
- TestProjectsSetBellRefusesABadValue: `--bell maybe` is a usage error (exit 2) and makes no daemon call.
- TestProjectsSetNeedsAtLeastOneFlagNamesBell: the usage message for no flag lists `--bell`.
- TestUsageTextNamesProjectsSetBell: `usageText` has `--bell on|off` and every line of it stays within 80 columns (the check at `internal/cli/upgrade_test.go:584` covers the width).

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests first and run them; each must fail for the reason given.
2. `internal/daemon/wire.go` and `handlers.go`: add the field, count it in `SetsNothing`, apply it in `setProject` under the same lock and busy check as `Push`. No new validation: a boolean needs none.
3. `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go`: add `bell := fs.String("bell", "", "on or off: ring the terminal bell for this project")`, parse it like `push`, add `--bell` to the no-flag message, and add `bell=on` / `bell=off` to the text line.
4. `internal/cli/cli.go`: add the flag to the `projects set` usage block only.
5. Docs: `docs/design.md` (wire row and paragraph: `--bell` takes `on` or `off`, `bell` in the wire list), `docs/guide.md` (table row: `--bell on|off`, the bell for the project's runs; the TUI reads it at start), `docs/state.md`.

7. Do not touch: `internal/tui`, `internal/registry` (S100 owns the field), `internal/engine`, `cmd`.
